body:
## Summary

This PR resolves two bugs in `url.pathToFileURL(filepath, options)` (`lib/internal/url.js`):

1. **Cross-platform root path double trailing slash (`file:////` and `file:///C://`)**:
   When preserving trailing slashes on directory inputs (`filePathLast === CHAR_FORWARD_SLASH || (windows && filePathLast === CHAR_BACKWARD_SLASH)`), `pathToFileURL` guarded against duplicating a root directory's existing separator by checking `resolved[resolved.length - 1] !== path.sep`. Because `path.sep` always reflects the **host OS** (`'\\'` on Windows, `'/'` on POSIX) rather than the **target platform** (`windows ? '\\' : '/'`), cross-platform calls with root paths failed this guard:
   - On a **Windows host** (`path.sep === '\\'`), `url.pathToFileURL('/', { windows: false })` resolves `'/'` via `path.posix.resolve('/')` to `'/'`, evaluates `'/' !== '\\'` (`true`), and appends an extra `'/'`, producing **`'file:////'`** (4 slashes) instead of **`'file:///'`**.
   - On a **POSIX host** (`path.sep === '/'`), `url.pathToFileURL('C:\\', { windows: true })` and `url.pathToFileURL('C:/', { windows: true })` resolve via `path.win32.resolve(...)` to `'C:\\'`, evaluate `'\\' !== '/'` (`true`), and append `'/'`, producing **`'file:///C://'`** instead of **`'file:///C:/'`**.

2. **Extended-length UNC path (`\\?\UNC\...`) with empty servername bypasses validation**:
   When parsing Windows UNC paths, `pathToFileURL` computes `const prefixLength = isExtendedUNC ? 8 : 2` (`2` for standard `\\server\share`, `8` for extended-length `\\?\UNC\server\share`) and searches for the next backslash starting at `prefixLength`: `const hostnameEndIndex = StringPrototypeIndexOf(resolved, '\\', prefixLength)`.
   However, the empty-servername check on line 1698 hardcoded `if (hostnameEndIndex === 2)` instead of `if (hostnameEndIndex === prefixLength)`. Consequently, passing an extended-length UNC path with an empty servername such as `url.pathToFileURL('\\\\?\\UNC\\\\share', { windows: true })` yielded `hostnameEndIndex = 8`, bypassed `8 === 2`, extracted an empty hostname (`resolved.slice(8, 8) === ''`), and silently returned **`URL { href: 'file:///share' }`** instead of throwing `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE` (`'Empty UNC servername'`).

Fixes: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/67091

---

---

## Deep-Dive Root Cause Analysis

### 1. Host `path.sep` Leakage into Cross-Platform Resolution (`lib/internal/url.js`, lines 1678–1716)

At the beginning of `pathToFileURL(filepath, options = kEmptyObject)`:

```js
const windows = options?.windows ?? isWindows;
let resolved = windows ?
  path.win32.resolve(filepath) :
  path.posix.resolve(filepath);
```

When `filepath` is a non-root directory path with a trailing slash (e.g., `'/dir/'` on POSIX or `'C:\\dir\\'` on Windows), `path.posix.resolve('/dir/')` strips the trailing slash and returns `'/dir'`, and `path.win32.resolve('C:\\dir\\')` strips the trailing backslash and returns `'C:\\dir'`. To preserve the directory semantics in the resulting `file:` URL, `pathToFileURL` appends `'/'` if `filepath` ended with a separator.

However, when `filepath` resolves to a **root directory** (`'/'` on POSIX or `'C:\\'` on Windows), `path.posix.resolve('/')` and `path.win32.resolve('C:\\')` **retain** their trailing separator (`'/'` and `'\\'`, respectively). To avoid appending a second slash to root paths, line 1713 checked:

```js
// BEFORE:
const filePathLast = StringPrototypeCharCodeAt(filepath,
                                               filepath.length - 1);
if ((filePathLast === CHAR_FORWARD_SLASH ||
     ((windows ?? isWindows) && filePathLast === CHAR_BACKWARD_SLASH)) &&
    resolved[resolved.length - 1] !== path.sep)
  resolved += '/';
```

There were two flaws in this condition:
1. **`resolved[resolved.length - 1] !== path.sep` checked the host's `path.sep` instead of the target platform's separator (`windows ? '\\' : '/'`)**:
   - When `windows` is `false` on a Windows host (`path.sep === '\\'`), `resolved` is `'/'`. Since `'/' !== '\\'` is `true`, `resolved` becomes `'//'`. Then `new URL('//', undefined, kCreateURLFromPosixPathSymbol)` encodes `'//'` into pathname `'//'`, producing `file:////`.
   - When `windows` is `true` on a POSIX host (`path.sep === '/'`), `resolved` is `'C:\\'`. Since `'\\' !== '/'` is `true`, `resolved` becomes `'C:\\/'`. Then `new URL('C:\\/', undefined, kCreateURLFromWindowsPathSymbol)` converts both separators into slashes, producing `file:///C://`.
2. **`(windows ?? isWindows)` was redundant**:
   - `windows` is already initialized on line 1678 as `const windows = options?.windows ?? isWindows;`, which is always a boolean (`true` or `false`), so `windows ?? isWindows` can never fall back to `isWindows`.

```js
// AFTER:
const filePathLast = StringPrototypeCharCodeAt(filepath,
                                               filepath.length - 1);
if ((filePathLast === CHAR_FORWARD_SLASH ||
     (windows && filePathLast === CHAR_BACKWARD_SLASH)) &&
    resolved[resolved.length - 1] !== (windows ? '\\' : '/'))
  resolved += '/';
```

---

### 2. Hardcoded Index `2` in Extended-Length UNC Validation (`lib/internal/url.js`, lines 1685–1706)

When `windows` is `true` and `resolved` starts with `'\\\\'`, `pathToFileURL` handles both standard UNC paths (`\\server\share`) and Win32 extended-length UNC paths (`\\?\UNC\server\share`):

```js
const isExtendedUNC = StringPrototypeStartsWith(resolved, '\\\\?\\UNC\\');
const prefixLength = isExtendedUNC ? 8 : 2;
const hostnameEndIndex = StringPrototypeIndexOf(
  resolved,
  '\\',
  prefixLength,
);
if (hostnameEndIndex === -1) {
  throw new ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE(
    'path',
    resolved,
    'Missing UNC resource path',
  );
}
if (hostnameEndIndex === 2) { // <-- BUG: hardcoded 2 instead of prefixLength!
  throw new ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE(
    'path',
    resolved,
    'Empty UNC servername',
  );
}
const hostname = StringPrototypeSlice(resolved, prefixLength, hostnameEndIndex);
```

- For a standard UNC path `'\\\\\\share'`, `isExtendedUNC` is `false`, `prefixLength` is `2`, and `StringPrototypeIndexOf('\\\\\\share', '\\', 2)` returns `2`. The check `hostnameEndIndex === 2` catches the empty servername and throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE` (`'Empty UNC servername'`).
- For an extended-length UNC path `'\\\\?\\UNC\\\\share'`, `isExtendedUNC` is `true` and `prefixLength` is `8`. Because `path.win32.resolve('\\\\?\\UNC\\\\share')` preserves the `\\\\?\\` prefix verbatim without collapsing consecutive backslashes, `resolved` is `'\\\\?\\UNC\\\\share'`.
- Calling `StringPrototypeIndexOf('\\\\?\\UNC\\\\share', '\\', 8)` finds the backslash at index `8` (`hostnameEndIndex === 8`).
- Because `8 === 2` evaluated to `false`, execution proceeded to `StringPrototypeSlice(resolved, 8, 8)`, which returned `''` (empty string) as the hostname, and constructed `file:///share` instead of throwing `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE`.
- Changing `if (hostnameEndIndex === 2)` to `if (hostnameEndIndex === prefixLength)` properly validates both standard (`prefixLength === 2`) and extended-length (`prefixLength === 8`) UNC paths.

---

## Step-by-Step Execution Trace (Before vs. After)

| Scenario | Input Call | Host OS | `resolved` after `path.*.resolve` | Guard Evaluation (Before) | Output (Before) | Guard Evaluation (After) | Output (After) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. POSIX root on Windows** | `pathToFileURL('/', { windows: false })` | Windows (`path.sep === '\\'`) | `'/'` | `'/' !== '\\'` (`true` -> appends `'/'`) | `'file:////'` ❌ | `'/' !== '/'` (`false`) | `'file:///'` ✅ |
| **2. Windows root (`\`) on POSIX** | `pathToFileURL('C:\\', { windows: true })` | POSIX (`path.sep === '/'`) | `'C:\\'` | `'\\' !== '/'` (`true` -> appends `'/'`) | `'file:///C://'` ❌ | `'\\' !== '\\'` (`false`) | `'file:///C:/'` ✅ |
| **3. Windows root (`/`) on POSIX** | `pathToFileURL('C:/', { windows: true })` | POSIX (`path.sep === '/'`) | `'C:\\'` | `'\\' !== '/'` (`true` -> appends `'/'`) | `'file:///C://'` ❌ | `'\\' !== '\\'` (`false`) | `'file:///C:/'` ✅ |
| **4. Extended UNC empty server** | `pathToFileURL('\\\\?\\UNC\\\\no-server', { windows: true })` | Any | `'\\\\?\\UNC\\\\no-server'` | `hostnameEndIndex === 2` (`8 === 2` -> `false`) | `'file:///no-server'` ❌ | `hostnameEndIndex === prefixLength` (`8 === 8` -> `true`) | Throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE` ✅ |

---

## Reproduction

```js
const assert = require('node:assert');
const url = require('node:url');

// 1. Cross-platform POSIX root path on Windows (or simulated)
assert.strictEqual(
  url.pathToFileURL('/', { windows: false }).href,
  'file:///'
);

// 2. Cross-platform Windows drive roots on POSIX (or simulated)
assert.strictEqual(
  url.pathToFileURL('C:\\', { windows: true }).href,
  'file:///C:/'
);
assert.strictEqual(
  url.pathToFileURL('C:/', { windows: true }).href,
  'file:///C:/'
);

// 3. Extended-length UNC path with empty servername
assert.throws(
  () => url.pathToFileURL('\\\\?\\UNC\\\\no-server', { windows: true }),
  {
    code: 'ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE',
    message: /Empty UNC servername/,
  }
);
```

---

## Test Coverage & Verification

- **`test/parallel/test-url-pathtofileurl.js`**:
  - Added `'\\\\?\\UNC\\\\no-server'` to the empty-server UNC `assert.throws` suite (`ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE`).
  - Added `{ path: 'C:\\', expected: 'file:///C:/' }` and `{ path: 'C:/', expected: 'file:///C:/' }` to `windowsTestCases` (which runs both with `{ windows: true }` on all platforms and natively on Windows).
  - Added `{ path: '/', expected: 'file:///' }` to `posixTestCases` (which runs both with `{ windows: false }` on all platforms and natively on POSIX).
- Verified all existing tests in `test/parallel/test-url-pathtofileurl.js` and Node.js ESLint rules pass with zero regressions.
